r: **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985** – added the **Tenth Schedule** (anti-defection law, **Defection**); amended **Arts 101, 102, 190 and 191**
Passed by Parliament **30-31 January 1985**; **Presidential assent 15 February 1985**
Curb defections “induced by the **lure of office**”; party discipline, stable governments; ban **floor crossing** by members elected on a party ticket
**First constitutional recognition of political parties** – the term “political party” appears in the Tenth Schedule
Members of **both Houses of Parliament and the State Legislatures** (MPs, MLAs, **MLCs**) – party, **independent** and **nominated** members
Not covered – the Schedule covers voting **in the House**; no binding whip in the electoral college
Sikkim's association with India – added by the **35th Amendment (1974)**, omitted by the **36th (1975)**
**“Aaya Ram Gaya Ram”** (Gaya Lal, **Haryana**); **Y.B. Chavan Committee** on defections (1967-69)
**Jammu and Kashmir** – first State with its own anti-defection law
AP: **Nadendla Bhaskara Rao** toppled **N.T. Rama Rao**'s government; NTR restored after a month
Union ministry ≤ **15% of Lok Sabha** strength
Disqualified defector barred from **Minister** / remunerative political post until re-elected
**Voluntarily gives up** party membership (inferred from conduct); **votes or abstains against the whip** without prior permission (**Para 2(1)(b)**)
Prior permission, or the party **condones within 15 days**
May become a Minister without joining a party
Joins a party **after six months** of taking his seat
May join **within six months**; not joining is no ground
May give up party membership on election to the Chair and **rejoin after demitting office**
Conduct such as campaigning for a rival party is enough (Ravi S. Naik 1994)
Does **not lose his seat**; still belongs to the party (G. Viswanathan 1996); sits as unattached; joining another party then = giving up membership
No disqualification when the **original party merges** with another and **not less than two-thirds** of its legislature party agree
**Deleted by the 91st Amendment (2003)** – a one-third group that breaks away is now disqualified

1.x: **En-bloc defections:** the law “banned only **retail** defections and legalised **wholesale** defections” – **en-bloc (bulk) defection** via merger is not covered; individual defection, defections in spells and votes against the whip are.
**Main criticism:** it stifles intra-party **dissent** and members' free expression, yet has not stopped mass defections – the two-thirds merger route can **defend mass defection**.

r: Powers, privileges and immunities of each House, its members and committees – Parliament / State Legislatures; free speech (105(1)) and immunity for anything said or voted (105(2))
Courts cannot inquire into proceedings for **irregularity of procedure**
**Not codified** in a single statute; rest on the Constitution, conventions (originally the House of Commons), rules, statutes and court rulings
Lok Sabha **Rule 222** / Rajya Sabha **Rule 187** – breach of privilege or contempt by a minister, member or outsider
Presiding Officer consents → House or **Privileges Committee** examines → the **House decides**
LS **15** members nominated by the Speaker; RS **10**, usually chaired by the **Deputy Chairman**
Publish its debates and proceedings; **restrain others** from publishing
**Freedom of speech** in the House and committees
**Freedom from arrest in civil cases** – during a session and **40 days** before and after; not in criminal or preventive detention cases
Make its own rules; regulate internal affairs
**Exemption from jury service**; may refuse to **attend as a witness** while the House sits
Receive **immediate information of a member's arrest**, detention, conviction or release
**Punish members and outsiders** for breach or contempt
No arrest or legal process within the **precincts** without the presiding officer's permission
**Reprimand, admonition, imprisonment** (only till the session ends); for members **suspension or expulsion** (seat declared vacant); **no fine**
Every breach is contempt, but not every contempt (e.g. disobeying a House order) is a breach of a specific privilege
Expulsion valid; privilege decisions reviewable only for **gross illegality or unconstitutionality**
7 judges: **no immunity for bribery** to speak or vote; overruled **P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998)**
Opinion **binding** (for MPs and State legislators alike)
**Final decision** on a Lok Sabha member's defection
Decided by **such member of the House as the House may elect** (Para 6(1))
The presiding officer acts on a member's petition – **no suo motu** case (Defection Rules 1985)
None in the Schedule; Speakers stay members of their parties – hence delays
**Struck down** in Kihoto – it needed State **ratification under Art. 368(2)**
Limited grounds – mala fides, perversity, natural justice, constitutional mandate
Tenth Schedule **valid** (no violation of free speech or basic structure); Para 7 struck down; **3:2**
Giving up membership ≠ resigning; inferred from conduct
Expelled member **still belongs** to the party
Upheld disqualification of **17** rebel MLAs; Speaker **cannot bar them from contesting**
Decide petitions ordinarily within **three months**; Parliament to consider a **permanent independent tribunal**
The **political party** (not the legislature party) appoints the whip and leader; legislators alone cannot bring a “**deemed merger**”
SC gave the Speaker a final **three weeks** for the last **2 of 10** BRS petitions
Bench of **P.S. Narasimha** and **Alok Aradhe**: gaps in Para 4 are “**matters for Parliament**”
Has not stopped defections; made **presiding officers** the deciders of defection cases (often criticised for partisan delay)
Legislators sequestered before a floor test to prevent poaching
MLAs **resign**, lowering the majority mark, and re-contest on the new party's ticket (**Karnataka 2019, MP 2020**)

**7 of 10 AAP** Rajya Sabha MPs claimed a merger with the BJP – cited as misuse of the merger exception
Disqualify only for **voluntarily giving up membership** or defying the whip on a **confidence motion**; decision by President/Governor on EC advice
Delete **both split and merger** exceptions; treat **pre-poll alliances** as parties
Defectors barred from office; **defector's vote invalid**
President/Governor to decide on the EC's binding advice
Limit the law to **confidence and money votes**
**Fixed timelines** for Speakers and an **independent tribunal** (SC, Keisham 2020)
